findings.message: `read_upload` joins a client-supplied name straight onto `UPLOAD_DIR`. A value like `../../etc/passwd` or an absolute path lets any caller read arbitrary files on the server.
The download handler never checks who is asking or whether that user owns the requested file. Even without traversal, anyone can fetch any other user's uploads by guessing names.

Several inputs crash the handler with an unhandled exception and an HTTP 500 instead of a proper error response. A missing file raises `FileNotFoundError`, an empty `file` parameter reads the directory and raises `IsADirectoryError`, and `.decode()` raises `UnicodeDecodeError` on binary uploads such as images.
This adds a new download endpoint and a new file-reading function but no test. The contributing guide requires a test for every change in behaviour.
